title: LossChart best-iteration line: no lower clamp and no NaN guard on bestIteration
description: bestX = bestIteration != null ? xScale(Math.min(bestIteration, lossHistory.length - 1)) : null. Two defects vs the hardened sibling: (1) no lower clamp -> a negative bestIteration yields a negative x and the dashed line is drawn off-canvas to the left; (2) `!= null` lets NaN through (NaN is not null) -> Math.min(NaN, n)=NaN -> xScale(NaN)=NaN -> a <line> with x1/x2=NaN is rendered, and the legend gains a spurious 'Best iter' entry. LossTab.tsx:100 uses `isFiniteNumber(bestIteration) ? xScale(Math.min(Math.max(bestIteration, 0), lossHistory.length - 1)) : null`, which clamps to [0, length-1] and rejects NaN. best_iteration is typed `number | null` (useNodeResultsStore.ts:56) and originates from the backend, so a NaN/negative value is a realistic wire input.
evidence: LossChart.tsx:49 lacks Math.max(_,0) and isFiniteNumber present in LossTab.tsx:100. NaN != null === true, so Number.NaN flows into xScale.
